newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold 1996 net profit up on Stop & Shop strength.
newsitem.headline: Ahold 1996 net profit up on Stop & Shop strength.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV said Thursday its 1996 earnings rose 39 percent on the strength of its U.S. Stop & Shop chain, and it expects significant earnings per share growth in 1997.
Chairman Cees van der Hoeven said most areas of the company saw improved profitability in 1996 and that the Stop & Shop supermarket chain significantly boosted earnings growth.
"On the other side of the ocean, our position in the U.S. was strengthened to such a degree that we can now speak of a solid base extending along virtually the entire East Coast," he said.

"The acquisition of Stop & Shop did not just lead to a new arithmetic increase, but to a geometric progression where whole new possibilities for profit improvement have opened up," Van der Hoeven said.
He said market shares increased in the United States and the Netherlands with significant productivity gains resulting from uses of new retail technologies.
Net profit in 1996 shot up 39 percent to $327.9 million, in line with forecasts. Revenues boomed to $18.9 billion from a year-earlier $15.4 billion.
"The consolidated result after taxes will be considerably higher in 1997 than in 1996. Earnings per share will also show significant growth in 1997," the company said.
Operating profit in the United States surged to $354.2 million, up 60 percent from $222 million in 1995.
